elites.name: evolvable-world-models
elites.title: Evolvable World Models for Open-Ended Biological Design
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems that can recursively refine and evolve their internal world models, inspired by biological evolution, will unlock novel avenues for open-ended design in synthetic biology and drug discovery.
elites.abstract: This research proposes developing AI agents capable of not only learning and refining world models but also evolving the very structure and mechanisms of these models over time, mirroring principles of open-ended biological evolution. Such 'evolvable world models' will be applied to complex biological design problems, such as de novo protein design and novel therapeutic development, accelerating discovery beyond human intuition.

elites.name: astrobiology_world_model_evolution
elites.title: Evolutionary World Models for Astrobiological Hypothesis Generation
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems will evolve internal world models specifically tuned for generating and testing hypotheses about extraterrestrial life and habitability.
elites.abstract: This research direction focuses on creating AI agents that not only refine their understanding of physical and chemical laws but also evolve novel conceptual frameworks for identifying biosignatures and assessing habitability in exoplanetary contexts. The agents will iteratively self-improve their world models through simulated exploration of diverse astrobiological scenarios, accelerating the discovery of plausible life-supporting conditions beyond Earth.

elites.name: evolvability_driven_discovery_ecosystems
elites.title: Evolvability-Driven Discovery Ecosystems for Scientific Paradigm Shifts
elites.short_hypothesis: AI agents designed with explicit mechanisms for evolving their own internal structures and communication protocols will autonomously discover entirely new scientific paradigms.
elites.abstract: Current AI discovery systems are constrained by human-designed architectures and fixed communication protocols, limiting their ability to generate truly novel scientific frameworks. This research proposes creating 'Evolvability-Driven Discovery Ecosystems' where AI agents can autonomously evolve their own internal representations, learning algorithms, and inter-agent communication strategies, fostering emergent, paradigm-shifting scientific breakthroughs.

elites.name: emergent_ecosystem_quality_diversity
elites.title: Evolutionary Quality-Diversity for Self-Assembling Scientific Ecosystems
elites.short_hypothesis: Applying evolutionary quality-diversity algorithms will enable AI agents to autonomously form diverse, specialized scientific sub-ecosystems that collectively achieve broader and more robust scientific progress than monolithic approaches.
elites.abstract: This research proposes leveraging evolutionary quality-diversity (QD) algorithms to guide the self-assembly of AI agents into distinct scientific 'niches' and sub-ecosystems, each optimized for different research methodologies or problem domains. By promoting diversity in agent capabilities and interaction strategies, these QD-driven ecosystems will unlock novel avenues of scientific discovery and accelerate progress beyond the limitations of current monolithic AI scientist frameworks.

elites.name: autogenetic_molecular_discovery
elites.title: Autogenetic Molecular Discovery: Self-Evolving Chemical Synthesizers
elites.short_hypothesis: AI systems that can autonomously design, synthesize, and test novel molecules, recursively refining their internal generative models based on experimental feedback, will dramatically accelerate materials science and drug discovery.
elites.abstract: Inspired by autopoiesis in biological systems, we propose AI agents that evolve their own molecular design and synthesis pipelines. These agents will learn from the outcomes of their chemical experiments to iteratively improve their generative models, enabling the discovery of molecules with unprecedented properties without direct human intervention.
